name: Charles River Laboratories
description: Charles River is an outsourced lab for drug developers: it breeds the research animals (mostly rodents, plus non-human primates), then does the discovery chemistry and regulated safety testing on them for a fee, and sells quality-control test kits to biologics makers. Services, not instruments, are the business: DSA is 60% of revenue and 18% margin, while the animal-model business earns 5% and Manufacturing Solutions lost $184 million in 2025 after goodwill and intangible write-downs, taking total operating income to just $25 million on $4.0 billion of revenue. A securities class action and government inquiries over its non-human-primate imports are open, and in November 2025 the board launched a strategic review that includes selling non-core assets worth about 7% of revenue.

employees.note: About 18,300 full-time and 1,400 part-time; about 2,400 science professionals with advanced degrees.

businessLines.name: Discovery and Safety Assessment (DSA)
businessLines.how: Charges drug developers fees per study for outsourced drug discovery, regulated toxicology and safety testing (including studies using animals), run at its own labs; revenue follows biopharma R&D spend and the backlog of booked studies.

businessLines.name: Research Models and Services (RMS)
businessLines.how: Breeds and sells laboratory rodents and other research models (and non-human primates) to pharma, biotech, academic and government labs, plus related services such as colony management; per-animal sales.

businessLines.name: Manufacturing Solutions
businessLines.how: Sells microbial detection and endotoxin-testing products and rapid-testing platforms (Microbial Solutions) used in quality control, and testing and development services for biologics and cell and gene therapy makers (Biologics Solutions); recurring consumables plus project services.

brands.name: Microbial Solutions and Biologics Solutions
brands.note: The two businesses of Manufacturing Solutions ($766.4M, 19.1% of revenue); individual revenue not broken out.

brands.name: K.F. (Cambodia) Ltd. assets
brands.note: Non-human primate supplier assets acquired January 2026; reported in DSA and RMS.

whatsNext.text: Strategic review announced in November 2025 includes divesting non-core assets representing about 7% of 2025 revenue; no completion dates given.
